newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU has two point plan to solve French EMU impasse.
newsitem.headline: EU has two point plan to solve French EMU impasse.

text.p: The European Commission will offer France a two-point compromise on Thursday to solve the new Socialist government's concerns about the European Union's post-single currency budget pact.

A Commission source told Reuters on Tuesday the French would be offered two resolutions attached to the so-called stability pact when it is discussed at the European Union summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17.
One resolution would talk about the coordination of economic policy. The other would address the bloc's coordination of employment policy.

At a meeting in Luxembourg on Monday, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told his EU partners that Paris needed time to study the stability pact, an integral part of EU plans for economic and monetary union (EMU).
The pact, agreed in principle in Dublin in December, is designed to keep EU budgets in order after EMU is launched on January 1, 1999.

The Commission's idea is to allow France to agree to the plan in Amsterdam by making it palatable politically through the resolutions spelling out the bloc's plans on economic and employment coordination.
France believes more attention must be paid to job creation and that governments must have a large role in monetary policy when the single currency is introduced.
But EU officials said the two resolutions would add little to what was already either EU policy or likely to be included in the new EU treaty due to be agreed at Amsterdam.
"All the instruments we need are already in the treaty," one senior official from an EU government said.
The employment resolution was expected to be effectively the same as the so-called Employment Chapter to be added to the treaty in Amsterdam.
This calls for some coordination of employment policy among EU members and makes creating jobs a formal goal of the Union.
The economic policy resolution will essentially be a restatement of a current EU treaty article laying out the areas where policy is to be coordinated, the Commission source said.
